paragraphs: We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing innovative cancer therapies. We currently have two commercially approved medicines, Revuforj® (revumenib) and Niktimvo (axatilimab-csfr), and a robust slate of clinical development programs designed to unlock the full potential of our first two products.

Revuforj is our first-in-class menin inhibitor that was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, in November 2024 for the treatment of relapsed or refractory, or R/R, acute leukemia with a lysine methyltransferase 2A gene, or KMT2A, translocation in adult and pediatric patients one year old and older. In October 2025, Revuforj received a second approval from the FDA for the treatment of R/R acute myeloid leukemia, or AML, with a susceptible nucleophosmin 1 mutation, or NPM1m, in adult and pediatric patients one year and older who have no satisfactory alternative treatment options. We are also studying revumenib in combination with standard-of-care agents in NPM1m AML and KMT2A-rearranged, or KMT2Ar, acute leukemia across the treatment landscape, including in newly diagnosed patients. Additionally, we are exploring the potential for menin inhibition in the treatment of myelofibrosis, or MF.

Niktimvo is our first-in-class colony stimulating factor-1 receptor, or CSF-1R, blocking antibody that was approved by the FDA in August 2024 for the treatment of chronic graft-versus-host disease, or cGVHD, after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg. Axatilimab is in development for the treatment of newly diagnosed cGVHD patients in combination with standard of care therapies, and for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, or IPF.

We licensed the global rights to revumenib and axatilimab, the first two FDA approved medicines to emerge from our pipeline. We are leading the commercialization and further development of revumenib and working closely with our collaboration partner, Incyte, on the commercialization and further development of axatilimab. We plan to continue to leverage the technical and business expertise of our management team and scientific collaborators to license, acquire and develop additional therapeutics to expand our pipeline.

• Successfully commercialize Revuforj in the U.S. for R/R acute leukemia patients with a KMT2A translocation and R/R AML patients with an NPM1 mutation; establish Revuforj as the preferred menin inhibitor, leveraging our first mover advantage and robust clinical data supporting the product's profile.

• Advance a robust pipeline of frontline trials of revumenib in combination with standard-of-care therapies to support potential additional listings in the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology, or NCCN Guidelines®, and/or label expansion opportunities.
• Evaluate opportunities to commercialize Revuforj outside of the United States, potentially on our own or in collaboration with partners who have operations and expertise outside the United States.
• Successfully commercialize Niktimvo in the U.S, in partnership with Incyte, for the treatment of cGVHD patients who have failed at least two prior lines of systemic therapy.
• Continue to advance clinical development programs designed to unlock the opportunity for Niktimvo to address newly diagnosed patients with cGVHD and other diseases, starting with IPF.

• Leverage the technical, clinical, regulatory and business expertise of our management team, scientific collaborators, and organization and network of advisors to license, acquire and develop additional cancer therapies to expand our pipeline and development plans.
We believe that strong execution of our strategy will position us to realize our mission to extend and improve the lives of cancer patients.

We have a product portfolio consisting of two FDA-approved products, Revuforj (revumenib) and Niktimvo (axatilimab-csfr), and a robust slate of clinical development programs designed to expand the opportunities for both medicines.
Revuforj in R/R Acute Leukemia with a KMT2A translocation

Revuforj is our oral, first-in-class menin inhibitor that was approved by the FDA in November 2024 for the treatment of R/R acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation in adult and pediatric patients one year and older. The approval was based on an FDA analysis of 104 patients with R/R acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation who were treated with Revuforj in the Phase 1/2 AUGMENT-101 trial. In the efficacy population, the rate of complete remission, or CR, plus CR with partial hematological recovery, or CRh, was 21% (22/104 pts; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 13.8%, 30.3%). The median duration of CR+CRh was 6.4 months (95% CI: 2.7, not estimable) and the median time to CR or CRh was 1.9 months (range: 0.9, 5.6 months). 23% (24/104 pts) of patients underwent hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, or HSCT, following treatment with Revuforj. Results from the 104-patient efficacy analysis are consistent with the previously reported, protocol-defined Phase 2 interim analysis of patients with R/R KMT2Ar acute leukemia in the AUGMENT-101 trial (n=57) which were published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in August 2024.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Industry

We have recently begun commercialization efforts and the sales, marketing, and distribution of Revuforj, Niktimvo, or any future approved products may be unsuccessful or less successful than anticipated.
If the market opportunities for our products are smaller than we believe they are, our revenue may be adversely affected, and our business may suffer.
We face significant competition from other biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, and our operating results will suffer if we fail to compete effectively.
We may incur additional costs or experience delays in completing, or ultimately be unable to complete, the development and commercialization of any of our product candidates.
If we or our collaborators are unable to enroll patients in clinical trials, these clinical trials may not be completed on a timely basis or at all.
We may be required to relinquish important rights to and control over the development and commercialization of our product candidates to our current or future collaborators.
We may explore strategic collaborations that may never materialize or may fail.
Disruptions at the FDA and other government agencies caused by layoffs, funding shortages or global health concerns could negatively impact our business.
Revuforj, Niktimvo and our future products may not achieve adequate market acceptance among physicians, patients, healthcare payors and others in the medical community to be commercially successful.
We are in the process of building and maintaining our sales, marketing and distribution infrastructure.
Our products and product candidates may face future development and regulatory difficulties.
Our failure to obtain regulatory approval in international jurisdictions would prevent us from marketing our product candidates outside the United States.

We have incurred significant operating losses since our inception. While we generate product revenue from sales of Revuforj and collaboration as well as milestone revenue from sales of Niktimvo, we continue to incur significant research and development and other expenses related to our ongoing operations. Except for 2021, we have not been profitable and have incurred losses in each period since our inception in 2005. For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, we reported a net loss of $285.4 million and $318.8 million, and $209.4 million, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $1.5 billion, which included non-cash charges for stock-based compensation, preferred stock accretion and extinguishment charges. As of December 31, 2025, we had cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $394.1 million.

Ongoing high interest rates could make it more difficult for us to obtain traditional financing on acceptable terms, if at all. Additionally, the ongoing recession risk together with the foregoing, could result in further economic uncertainty and volatility in the capital markets in the near term and, as a result could negatively affect our operations. Furthermore, such economic conditions have produced downward pressure on share prices. Although we do not believe that inflation has had a material impact on our financial position or results of operations to date, the return of a high inflationary environment could increase our operating costs, including our labor costs and research and development costs. These costs may also be negatively impacted due to supply chain constraints, global geopolitical tensions, worsening macroeconomic conditions and employee availability and wage increases, which may result in additional stress on our working capital.

Additionally, we are subject to other challenges and risks specific to our business and our ability to execute on our strategy, as well as risks and uncertainties common to companies in the pharmaceutical industry with development and commercial operations, including, without limitation, risks and uncertainties associated with: obtaining regulatory approval of our late-stage product candidate; identifying, acquiring or in-licensing additional products or product candidates; pharmaceutical product development and the inherent uncertainty of clinical success; the challenges of protecting and enhancing our intellectual property rights; and complying with applicable regulatory requirements.

Our second FDA-approved product, Revuforj, was approved by the FDA for commercial sale in the U.S. on November 15, 2024. Net product revenue from sales of Revuforj was $124.8 million and $7.7 million for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 respectively. In accordance with GAAP, we determine net product revenue for Revuforj, with specific assumptions for variable consideration components including, but not limited to, trade discounts and allowances, co-pay assistance programs and payor rebates. We record product revenue net of estimated discounts, chargebacks, rebates, product returns, and other gross-to-net revenue deductions.
We generated no net product revenue during the year ended December 31, 2023.

In September 2021, we entered into the Incyte License and Collaboration Agreement, or the Incyte License, with Incyte covering the worldwide development and commercialization of axatilimab. In August 2024, the FDA approved Niktimvo for the treatment of cGVHD after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kg (88.2 lbs). Niktimvo sales began in February 2025.

In accordance with Topic ASC 808, Collaboration Arrangements, Incyte has been identified as the principal in product sales, therefore, we will recognize its 50% share of any profits or losses in the amount of net product sales less cost of goods sold and shared commercial and other expenses, including any royalties owed on license agreements, in the period in which the underlying sales and costs are recognized. Our share of net profits in connection with commercialization of Niktimvo will be presented as "Collaboration revenue, net" and our share of net losses will be presented as "Collaboration loss" within operating expenses. We will continue to recognize the costs associated with ongoing development services in the R&D operating expense line, including any cost-sharing components with Incyte.

We enter into license agreements for the development and commercialization of our product candidates. License agreements may include non-refundable upfront payments, contingent milestone and/or royalty payments based on the occurrence of specified events under our license arrangements, partial or complete reimbursement of research and development expenses, license fees and royalties on sales if they are successfully approved and commercialized. Our performance obligations under the license agreements may include the transfer of intellectual property rights in the form of licenses, obligations to provide research and development services and related materials and participation on certain development and/or commercialization committees.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家商業階段的生物製藥公司，致力於開發創新性癌症治療方案。本公司目前擁有兩項已上市的藥物，Revuforj®（revumenib）與 Niktimvo（axatilimab-csfr），並有一系列強大的臨牀開發計畫，旨在發揮本公司前兩項產品的完整潛力。

Revuforj 為本公司第一個上市的 menin 抑製劑，於 2024 年 11 月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准，用於治療具有 lysine methyltransferase 2A 基因（KMT2A）轉位的復發性或難治性（R/R）急性白血病患者，年齡為一歲以上之成人及兒童。於 2025 年 10 月，Revuforj 又獲 FDA 批准，用於治療具有 susceptible nucleophosmin 1 突變（NPM1m）的復發性或難治性急性骨髓性白血病（AML）患者，年齡為一歲以上之成人及兒童，且無滿意的替代治療選擇。本公司亦正在研究 revumenib 與標準療法藥物合併使用於 NPM1m AML 及 KMT2A-rearranged（KMT2Ar）急性白血病患者，包括新診斷患者。此外，本公司亦在探討 menin 抑製劑在治療骨髓纖維化（MF）方面的潛力。
Niktimvo 為本公司第一個上市的 colony stimulating factor-1 受體（CSF-1R）阻斷單株抗體，於 2024 年 8 月獲 FDA 批准，用於治療慢性移植物抗宿主病（cGVHD）患者，這些患者已於至少兩線系統性治療失敗後。Axatilimab 正在開發中，用於治療新診斷的 cGVHD 患者，與標準療法藥物合併使用，以及用於治療特發性肺纖維化（IPF）。
本公司已取得 revumenib 與 axatilimab 全球權利，這兩項藥物為本公司產品線中首度獲 FDA 批准的藥物。本公司正領導 revumenib 的商業化與進一步開發，並與合作夥伴 Incyte 密切合作進行 axatilimab 的商業化與進一步開發。本公司計畫持續利用管理團隊與科學合作夥伴的技術與商業專業知識，以取得、收購並開發更多治療藥物，以擴充本公司產品線。
• 成功於美國商業化 Revuforj，用於治療具有 KMT2A 轉位的 R/R 急性白血病患者及具有 NPM1 突變的 R/R AML 患者；建立 Revuforj 為首選的 menin 抑製劑，利用本公司首創優勢與強大的臨牀數據支持產品特性。
• 推動 revumenib 與標準療法藥物合併使用的首線臨牀試驗，以支持潛在的 NCCN 臨牀實務指引（NCCN Guidelines®）新增 listing 以及標籤擴張機會。
• 評估於美國以外地區商業化 Revuforj 的機會，可能自行進行或與在美國以外地區擁有運作與專業知識的合作夥伴合作。
• 成功於美國商業化 Niktimvo，與 Incyte 合作，用於治療已於至少兩線系統性治療失敗的 cGVHD 患者。
• 繼續推進臨牀開發計畫，以挖掘 Niktimvo 解決新診斷的 cGVHD 及其他疾病患者的機會，首先從 IPF 開始。
• 藉由我們管理團隊、科學合作夥伴以及組織與顧問網路的技術、臨牀、法規與商業專業知識，取得、收購並開發更多癌症治療藥物，以擴展我們的藥物研發管道與發展計畫。
我們認為，強力執行我們的策略，將使我們能實現我們的使命，即延長並改善癌症患者的生存品質。
我們的產品組合包含兩種美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准的產品，Revuforj（revumenib）與 Niktimvo（axatilimab-csfr），以及一系列強大的臨牀開發計畫，以擴展兩種藥物的應用機會。
Revuforj 用於治療具有 KMT2A 轉位的 R/R 急性白血病

Revuforj 是我們的口服、第一類 menin 抑制劑，於 2024 年 11 月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）核准，用於治療具有 KMT2A 轉位的 R/R 急性白血病，適用於年齡一歲以上之成人及兒童患者。此核准是基於 FDA 對 104 名患有 R/R 急性白血病且具有 KMT2A 轉位的患者，在 Phase 1/2 AUGMENT-101 試驗中接受 Revuforj 治療的分析。在療效族羣中，完全緩解（CR）或完全緩解伴隨部分血液學恢復（CRh）的發生率為 21%（22/104 位患者；95% 信心區間 [CI]：13.8%，30.3%）。CR+CRh 的中位持續時間為 6.4 個月（95% CI：2.7，無法估計），而達到 CR 或 CRh 的中位時間為 1.9 個月（範圍：0.9，5.6 個月）。23%（24/104 位患者）的患者在接受 Revuforj 治療後進行造血幹細胞移植（HSCT）。來自 104 位患者的療效分析結果與先前報告的、AUGMENT-101 試驗中 R/R KMT2Ar 急性白血病患者的協議定義 Phase 2 期中分析結果一致（n=57），該分析於 2024 年 8 月發表在《臨牀腫瘤學雜誌》（Journal of Clinical Oncology）上。

我們是一家商業階段的生物製藥公司，致力於開發創新癌症治療方案。目前我們擁有兩種已上市的藥物，Revuforj®（revumenib）與Niktimvo（axatilimab-csfr），以及一項強大的臨牀開發計畫，旨在充分發揮我們前兩種產品的潛力。

Revuforj 是我們第一個上市的 menin 抑製劑，於2024年11月獲美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）批准，用於治療具有 lysine methyltransferase 2A 基因（KMT2A）轉位的復發或難治性（R/R）急性白血病，適用於年齡一歲以上之成人與兒童患者。2025年10月，Revuforj 又獲得 FDA 批准，用於治療具有 susceptible nucleophosmin 1 mutation（NPM1m）的 R/R 急性骨髓性白血病（AML），適用於年齡一歲以上且無滿意替代治療選擇的成人與兒童患者。我們也在研究 revumenib 與標準療法藥物結合使用，用於 NPM1m AML 與 KMT2A-rearranged（KMT2Ar）急性白血病的治療，包括新診斷的患者。此外，我們也在探討 menin 抑製劑在治療骨髓纖維化（MF）上的潛力。

Niktimvo 是我們第一個上市的 colony stimulating factor-1 receptor（CSF-1R）阻斷單株抗體，於2024年8月獲 FDA 批准，用於治療慢性移植物抗宿主疾病（cGVHD），適用於在至少兩種系統性治療失敗後的成人與體重至少40公斤的兒童患者。Axatilimab 正在開發中，用於治療新診斷的 cGVHD 患者，與標準療法藥物結合使用，以及用於治療特發性肺纖維化（IPF）。
我們已取得 revumenib 與 axatilimab 的全球權利，這兩種藥物是我們產品線中首度獲 FDA 批准的藥物。我們正在領導 revumenib 的商業化與進一步開發，並與合作夥伴 Incyte 密切合作，進行 axatilimab 的商業化與進一步開發。我們計畫持續利用管理團隊與科學合作夥伴的技術與商業專業知識，以取得、收購並開發更多治療方案，以擴展我們的產品線。

自我們成立以來，我們已產生顯著的營運虧損。雖然我們從 Revuforj 的銷售與合作，以及 Niktimvo 的銷售中產生產品收入與里程碑收入，我們仍持續產生與營運相關的大量研究與開發及其他費用。除了2021年外，我們尚未實現盈利，自2005年成立以來每個期間均產生虧損。截至2025年12月31日，我們報告的淨虧損為285.4百萬美元與318.8百萬美元，以及2023年為209.4百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，我們的累積虧損為1.5十億美元，其中包括股票選擇權的非現金費用、優先股累計與贖回費用。截至2025年12月31日，我們持有現金、現金等價物與短期投資共394.1百萬美元。

持續高利率可能使我們更難以在可接受的條件下取得傳統融資，甚至無法取得。此外，持續的經濟衰退風險加上上述因素，可能導致近期資本市場出現進一步的經濟不確定性與波動，因此可能對我們的營運產生負面影響。此外，這些經濟情況已對股價產生向下壓力。儘管我們不認為通貨膨脹對我們的財務狀況或營運結果迄今有重大影響，但若出現高通貨膨脹環境，可能會提高我們的營運成本，包括勞動成本與研究與開發成本。這些成本也可能因供應鏈限制、全球地緣政治緊張、惡化總體經濟條件與員工可得性與工資上漲而受到負面影響，這可能導致我們營運資金出現額外壓力。
此外，我們面臨其他挑戰與風險，這些風險與我們的業務及我們執行策略的能力有關，也與藥品產業中公司常見的風險與不確定性有關，包括但不限於：取得我們晚期產品候選藥物的監管批准；識別、取得或取得授權額外的產品或產品候選藥物；藥品產品開發及臨牀成功固有的不確定性；保護與強化我們智慧財產權的挑戰；以及遵守適用的監管要求。

本公司第二項獲得美國食品藥物管理局核准的產品 Revuforj，於 2024 年 11 月 15 日獲准在美國商業販售。Revuforj 的淨產品收入分別為 124.8 百萬美元及 7.7 百萬美元，係指截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日之十二個月期間。根據一般會計準則，本公司針對 Revuforj 的淨產品收入進行計算，並針對變動考量要素，包括但不限於貿易折扣與允許條件、共付協助計畫及付款人退費，設有特定假設。本公司將產品收入扣除預估的折扣、回扣、退費、產品退貨及其他毛利轉淨收入扣除項目後入賬。
我們在2023年12月31日止年度中，未產生任何淨產品收入。
2021年9月，我們與Incyte簽訂了Incyte授權與合作協議，或稱Incyte授權，涵蓋axatilimab在全球的開發與商業化。2024年8月，FDA核准Niktimvo用於治療cGVHD，此症狀為在成人及體重至少40公斤（88.2磅）的兒童患者中，對至少兩種先前系統治療失敗後的治療。Niktimvo的銷售於2025年2月開始。

根據ASC 808主題，合作安排，Incyte被認定為產品銷售的主體，因此，我們將在產品銷售淨收入減去商品成本及共享商業及其他費用，包括任何根據授權協議應支付的版稅，於銷售及成本認列的期間，認列其50%的任何利潤或損失。我們與Niktimvo商業化相關的淨利潤部分，將列示為「合作收入，淨額」，而淨損失部分將列示為「合作損失」於營運費用中。我們將繼續在研發營運費用項目中認列與持續開發服務相關的成本，包括與Incyte的任何成本分擔部分。
我們與開發與商業化產品候選藥物的授權協議。授權協議可能包括不可退款的預付金、根據我們授權安排中指定事件發生而支付的條件性里程碑及/或版稅付款、部分或全部補償研究與開發費用、授權費及銷售成功核准與商業化後的版稅。我們在授權協議下的履行義務可能包括以授權形式轉移智慧財產權、提供研究與開發服務及相關材料的義務，以及參與某些開發及/或商業化委員會。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關的風險
我們近期已開始商業化努力，Revuforj、Niktimvo 或任何未來核准產品的銷售、行銷及分銷可能不如預期成功或較預期成功。
若我們產品的市場機會小於我們所認為的，我們的營業收入可能受到負面影響，且我們的業務可能受損。
我們面臨來自其他生物科技與製藥公司的重大競爭，若我們無法有效競爭，我們的營運結果將受影響。
我們可能產生額外成本或遭遇延宕，或最終無法完成任何產品候選藥物的開發與商業化。
若我們或我們的合作夥伴無法於臨牀試驗中納入病患，這些臨牀試驗可能無法按時或完全完成。
我們可能必須放棄對產品候選藥物開發與商業化的重要權利與控制權，以給我們現有或未來的合作夥伴。
本公司可能探討策略性合作夥伴關係，但這些合作關係可能無法實現或可能失敗。
美國食品藥物管理局及其他政府機構因裁員、經費不足或全球健康議題所造成的幹擾，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
Revuforj、Niktimvo 及本公司未來產品可能無法在醫界取得足夠的市場接受度，包括醫生、病人、醫療付費者及其他相關人士，因而無法實現商業成功。
本公司正在建立並維護銷售、行銷及分銷基礎設施。
本公司產品及產品候選藥物可能面臨未來的開發及監管困難。
本公司若無法取得國際管轄區域的監管批准，將無法在美國以外地區推廣產品候選藥物。
paragraphs: 本年度報告包含根據我們目前預期所提出的展望性資訊。因為我們的業務面臨許多風險，而實際結果可能與任何由我們或代表我們所做出的展望性陳述有重大差異，本節包含可能影響我們業務、營運結果、財務狀況以及我們普通股交易價格的重要因素討論。您應仔細考慮這些風險因素，並與本年度報告中包含的所有其他資訊以及我們向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）公開提交的其他文件一併參考。
我們的業務面臨許多風險與不確定性，您在決定投資我們證券前應注意這些風險與不確定性。這些風險與不確定性包括但不限於以下內容：
• 我們的業務嚴重依賴我們能否成功在美國及其他我們可能獲得上市許可的司法管轄區商業化Revuforj與Niktimvo。沒有保證我們針對Revuforj或Niktimvo的商業化努力會成功，或我們將能按預期的水準與時間點產生收入。
• 我們最近才開始商業化努力，Revuforj、Niktimvo或任何未來核准產品的銷售、行銷與分銷可能未如預期成功或較預期為不成功。
• 若我們產品的市場機會小於我們所預期，我們的收入可能受到不利影響，而我們的業務可能遭受損失。
• 我們面臨來自其他生物科技與製藥公司的重大競爭，若我們無法有效競爭，我們的營運結果將受影響。
